questions.scenario: A wild monkey suddenly enters the school ground during the morning assembly. Chaos breaks out! What do you do?

options.A: Run closer to the action with your phone out, trying to record the exact moment the monkey steals the PT Sir's whistle.
options.B: Observe the boundary walls and trees to figure out exactly how the monkey bypassed the school's high-security fencing.
options.C: Grab the microphone from the podium and start giving a dramatic, live running commentary of the situation to entertain the crowd.
options.D: Quickly coordinate with the class monitors to form a safe corridor so the junior kids can exit without panicking.

questions.scenario: There is a massive rumor spreading that the Principal is cancelling the highly anticipated Class 10 trip to Manali. How do you react?

options.A: Sneak around the staff room during recess to overhear the teachers' conversations and catch any live updates.
options.B: Cross-check the school calendar, read past circulars, and quietly interrogate the Head Boy to find out the actual truth.
options.C: Become the main storyteller of your friend group, narrating the rumor with full suspense, dramatic pauses, and expressions.
options.D: Tell everyone to stop panicking and wait for you to officially confirm the news with the class teacher before reacting.

questions.scenario: Your Chacha (uncle) forwards a wild WhatsApp message in the Family Group claiming the 'National Anthem is declared best by UNESCO'.

options.A: You jump into the chat instantly, asking rapid-fire questions about who sent it to him and trying to track the source of the forward.
options.B: You immediately do a Google search, find a trusted fact-check article, and send screenshots proving the news is 100% fake.
options.C: You record a hilarious, dramatic voice note reading out the fake forward in a serious news-reader voice and send it to your cousins.
options.D: You step in politely but firmly, calm the uncles down, and suggest a new 'no fake forwards' rule for the family group.

questions.scenario: It's the deadline day for the annual School Magazine. Everyone is stressed. What is your main contribution?

options.A: Rushing to the school canteen to get an exclusive, last-minute interview with the canteen bhaiya about the rising samosa prices.
options.B: Reading through every single submitted article with a red pen, hunting for spelling mistakes, plagiarized text, and factual errors.
options.C: Posing for the vibrant cover photo and writing a catchy, emotional introduction note that will make everyone want to read it.
options.D: Sitting with the design team, deciding which articles make the final cut, and finalizing the overall page layout.

questions.scenario: It's PTM (Parent-Teacher Meeting) day, and the vibe outside the classroom is incredibly tense. What are you doing?

options.A: Eavesdropping on the intense conversation between the strict math teacher and your friend's parents to get the 'inside scoop'.
options.B: Mentally calculating your internal marks, reviewing your test papers, and preparing a logical, foolproof defense for your low grades.
options.C: Putting on your most confident smile, making eye contact, and using your charm to smoothly talk your way out of the teacher's complaints.
options.D: Strategizing with your friends on exactly what order to go inside to minimize the teacher's anger and manage your parents' mood.

questions.scenario: Someone's expensive geometry box gets stolen during the lunch break. The class doors are locked. How do you solve it?

options.A: Start physically checking the backbenches and dustbins, actively looking for where the thief might have thrown it.
options.B: Notice who stayed back in class during the PT period, connect their behavior, and logically narrow down the suspects.
options.C: Stand on a desk and make a powerful public appeal, urging the 'culprit' to do the right thing and return it anonymously.
options.D: Take charge of the room, tell everyone to stay in their seats, and organize a systematic, fair search with the class monitor.

questions.scenario: Your city suddenly declares a 'Bandh' (strike) and school is closed. You have an unexpected day off. What do you do?

options.A: Go straight to the balcony or terrace to get a first-hand look at the empty streets or passing rallies in your neighborhood.
options.B: Scroll through Twitter and local news portals to figure out the deep political reason behind why the strike was actually called.
options.C: Set up your phone ring-light and record a chatty, entertaining vlog about your 'unexpected day off' experience for Instagram.
options.D: Draft a brand new schedule for the day, deciding exactly how to divide these 8 free hours between studying, gaming, and relaxing.

questions.scenario: Your housing society is having a massive, heated argument about the DJ timings for the upcoming Diwali party. You...

options.A: Stand right in the middle of the arguing uncles, subtly recording the drama on your phone to show your friends later.
options.B: Quickly dig up the official municipal rules on noise pollution on your phone to see which side is legally correct.
options.C: Take the mic from the DJ and make a smooth, persuasive, and funny speech that instantly lightens the mood and unites the crowd.
options.D: Intervene as the mediator, propose a fair compromise of 10 PM, and get both the youth and the elders to agree to your plan.

questions.scenario: During an inter-school debate competition, your opposing team makes a completely wild, made-up claim. How do you react?

options.A: Interrupt them aggressively during the rebuttal round, demanding they show immediate proof of what they just said.
options.B: Quietly pull out your reference cards, find the exact statistic that proves them wrong, and destroy their argument with pure facts.
options.C: Use sarcasm, excellent voice modulation, and dramatic expressions to make the audience laugh at their ridiculous point.
options.D: Signal your teammates to change the debate strategy on the spot, shifting the focus to a topic where your team is stronger.

questions.scenario: You are organizing the Teachers' Day celebration. What is your primary responsibility?

options.A: Running around the auditorium with a camera, capturing candid shots of the teachers laughing and the students performing.
options.B: Secretly interviewing students to collect funny but accurate trivia about each teacher for the 'Guess the Teacher' game.
options.C: Being the main stage anchor! You wear a crisp outfit, hold the mic perfectly, and deliver the welcome speech flawlessly.
options.D: Managing the entire event timeline, making sure the cake arrives on time, the mic is working, and the performances are in order.

Role_1.title: Field Reporter / Photojournalist
Role_1.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate action-taker! You have zero stage fright, love being on the ground, and have a natural instinct to run towards the action while everyone else is running away. You want to show the world what's happening right now.
Role_1.day_in_the_life: Rushing to the scene of a breaking news event (like a flood, election rally, or sports match), holding the mic in extreme conditions, interviewing eyewitnesses on the spot, and capturing powerful photographs.
Role_1.alternative_match_text: Your high energy, bravery, and on-the-go lifestyle also make you a great fit for Event Management, Travel Vlogging, or Public Relations.
Role_1.roadmap: Take Arts/Humanities in 11th and 12th. Pursue a Bachelor of Journalism and Mass Communication (BJMC) or BA in Mass Media. Focus heavily on internships with local newspapers or news channels during college to build your ground-reporting portfolio!

Role_2.title: Investigative Journalist / Fact-Checker
Role_2.primary_match_text: You have the brain of a detective! You don't believe things at face value. You love digging deep, finding hidden loopholes, cross-checking facts, and exposing the truth. You are the enemy of fake news.
Role_2.day_in_the_life: Spending weeks reading through government documents, finding proof of corporate scams, interviewing secret whistleblowers, and writing highly detailed, evidence-backed articles that can change society.
Role_2.alternative_match_text: Your highly analytical mind and research skills make you perfect for Law, Data Analytics, Criminology, or Academic Research.
Role_2.roadmap: Arts, Commerce, or Science—any stream works in 11th/12th, but Arts is preferred. Pursue a BA in Journalism or Political Science. After graduation, look for a Post-Graduate Diploma in Investigative Journalism or Data Journalism. Learn to use RTI (Right to Information) effectively!

Role_3.title: TV Anchor / News Presenter
Role_3.primary_match_text: You are the charismatic face of the news! You have a powerful voice, excellent communication skills, and the confidence to hold the attention of millions of viewers. You know how to make words sound impactful.
Role_3.day_in_the_life: Sitting in a high-tech studio, reading the teleprompter flawlessly, modulating your voice for breaking news, and conducting heated live debates with politicians and experts on prime-time television.
Role_3.alternative_match_text: Your strong public speaking and magnetic personality also make you a fantastic fit for Acting, Radio Jockeying (RJ), Podcasting, or Corporate Communications.
Role_3.roadmap: Choose Arts/Humanities with a strong focus on English or Hindi literature in 11th/12th. Pursue a BJMC (Bachelor of Journalism and Mass Communication). Participate heavily in college debates, theatre, and public speaking clubs to polish your voice and screen presence.

Role_4.title: Chief Editor / News Producer
Role_4.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate newsroom boss! You have a great 'news sense'—you know exactly what the public wants to read or watch. You are a natural leader who can manage a chaotic team under strict deadlines.
Role_4.day_in_the_life: Leading the morning editorial meeting, deciding which story gets the front page or prime-time slot, editing reporters' articles for perfection, and managing the overall budget and strategy of the news organization.
Role_4.alternative_match_text: Your leadership, decision-making, and organizational skills translate perfectly to Management, Publishing, Content Strategy, or Film Direction.
Role_4.roadmap: Take Arts or Commerce in 11th/12th. Complete your BJMC or BA in English/Mass Comm. To become an editor, you need years of experience, but pursuing a Master's degree (MJMC) from top institutes like IIMC (Indian Institute of Mass Communication) or AJK MCRC will give you a massive head start in the industry.
